records.quote: (sine) any angle equals (cosine) the supplementary
records.claim: The sine of any angle equals the cosine of the supplementary (complementary) angle of this angle, and vice versa.
records.notes: Printed word 'supplementary' though meaning complementary; recorded as printed.

records.quote: for example: sin 30° = cos 60°, cos 30° = sin 60°
records.text: for example: sin 30° = cos 60°, cos 30° = sin 60° and sin 45° = cos 45°.

records.quote: For any angle A : tan A = sin A / cos A
records.claim: For any angle A, tan A = sin A / cos A.

records.label: Example
records.quote: Connecting with Geometry: ABC is an isosceles triangle
records.stem: Connecting with Geometry: ABC is an isosceles triangle in which AB = AC = 8 cm and BC = 12 cm. Find: First: $m(\angle B)$. Second: The area of the surface of the triangle to the nearest two decimal numbers.
solution: ∵ The triangle ABC is an isosceles triangle.

parts.label: Second
parts.stem: The area of the surface of the triangle to the nearest two decimal numbers.

records.quote: A, C, D, B with 8 cm, 6 cm
records.caption: Isosceles triangle ABC with apex A, base CB; AB and AC each marked 8 cm; AD drawn perpendicular to CB with D on CB and right angle marked; CD = 6 cm, DB = 6 cm.

records.quote: D the midpoint of BC and BD = CD = 6 cm
records.text: $\therefore$ D the midpoint of $\overline{BC}$ and BD = CD = 6 cm; $\because \cos B = \frac{6}{8} = \frac{3}{4} = 0.75$

records.quote: Using the calculator :
records.text: Using the calculator: SHIFT cos 0.75 = ° ' '' ; $\therefore m(\angle B) = 41° 24' 35''$ (Q.E.D 1)

records.quote: To find the surface area of the triangle : find AD
records.text: To find the surface area of the triangle: find AD (From Pythagoras' theorem). $(AD)^2=(AB)^2-(BD)^2$; $(AD)^2 = 64-36=28$; $AD=2\sqrt{7}$. The area of the triangle ABC $=\frac12\times BC\times AD=\frac12\times 12\times 2\sqrt7 = 12\sqrt7$ cm$^2 \simeq 31.75$ cm$^2$ (Q.E.D. 2)
records.notes: Continues solution of previous example; 'Phythegoran's' misspelt in print.

records.quote: Another solution for the second part:
records.text: Another solution for the second part:

records.quote: sin B = AD/AB ... AD = 8 sin (41° 24' 35'')
records.text: $\because \sin B=\frac{AD}{AB}$, $\therefore \sin B=\frac{AD}{8}$, $\therefore AD = 8\sin(41°24'35'')$ (1). The area of the triangle ABC $=\frac12\times BC\times AD$, substitute from (1) in this relation: $\therefore$ area $=\frac12\times12\times8\sin(41°24'35'')\simeq 31.75$ cm$^2$.
